acceptance: The stable package exports the classified_as relation plus a source-specific endpoint-pair table for governs and requires with derived from and to sets, without framework, model-provider, or database coupling.

Deterministic edge validation keeps rejecting incompatible endpoints for every relation: permission -> entity, datapolicy -> action, and permission -> datapolicy stay rejected, while datapolicy -> entity and requirement -> datapolicy are accepted.

Deterministic governance validation reports conflicting classification, an entity whose classification requires a handling policy but has none, and a policy that permits continuous export of secret or regulated data, each with a stable error code.

Issue collection remains total and deterministic across repeated runs, node and edge insertion orders, and JSON object key orders, under the documented core -> node -> edge -> relation -> governance phase order and sort key.
Domain validation does not mutate, reorder, or normalize its input, and well-formed Product Graph v1 canonical revision identity is unchanged by domain validation.
Focused relation and governance tests plus the full repository format, lint, typecheck, and test suites pass on the exact candidate, and Ubuntu and Windows CI both pass.
Diffcipline exact-candidate proof, Alibaba OCR deterministic accounting/rule resolution with semantic review, and Jev typed judgments are recorded before guarded merge.

required: Stable @ineractive/product-graph source-specific endpoint pairs plus the classified_as relation and the deterministic governance rules with focused tests.
Proof that every endpoint combination rejected before this Grain is still rejected and that canonical revision identity is unchanged for well-formed documents.
Exact-candidate Diffcipline proof, Alibaba OCR deterministic accounting/rule resolution with semantic review, and Jev typed judgments.
Exact-head Ubuntu and Windows repository CI plus post-merge fresh-main qualification.

minimality.rationale: Extend the already-qualified stable package with one bounded endpoint-pair table, one new relation, and one governance validation phase plus focused tests, instead of adding a package, promoting the prototype lab, or introducing a runtime dependency.

requirements: Governance validation composes on top of the SG-000020 node layer, the SG-000021 edge and relation layer, the SG-000022 classification and lifecycle layer, and the Product Graph v1 core contract, and must never weaken or bypass any of them.
Deterministic validation must not depend on object iteration accidents, wall-clock time, randomness, network calls, or model inference.
The endpoint-pair refactor must not relax any existing endpoint check: every endpoint combination rejected before this Grain must still be rejected.
Declaring a classification or a governance relation must never be presented as legal or regulatory compliance, and no validator may claim compliance.

outcome: The stable @ineractive/product-graph domain layer declares allowed endpoint pairs as the single endpoint authority, adds the classified_as classification relation, gives governs the source-specific pairs permission -> action and datapolicy -> entity, extends requires to requirement -> datapolicy, and adds a deterministic governance phase that reports an entity classified into conflicting classes, an entity whose classification requires a handling policy but has none, and a data policy that permits continuous export of secret or regulated data.
rationale: SG-000022 delivered the classification and lifecycle node layer of IN-P02-S02-T02 and explicitly deferred the classification and governance relations plus the cross-node rules to this dependent Grain.

risk.recovery: Revert the SG-000023 endpoint-pair table, the classified_as relation, the extended governs and requires targets, the governance phase and its rules, the focused tests, the evidence record, and the current-frontier update; the SG-000022 classification and lifecycle node layer, the SG-000020 and SG-000021 node, edge, and relation layer, the Product Graph v1 contracts, and ADR-0003 remain intact and no production state is mutated.

scope_in: Extend the domain edge-kind spec with explicit allowed endpoint pairs as the single endpoint authority, deriving the declared from and to sets from the pair table so one relation name can carry source-specific targets without weakening any existing endpoint check.
Declare the classified_as relation from an entity to a dataclass, extend governs to the pairs permission -> action and datapolicy -> entity, and extend requires to requirement -> datapolicy.
Add the governance phase after the relation phase and the stable error code DOMAIN_CONFLICTING_CLASSIFICATION for an entity classified into more than one distinct level.

Add the stable error code DOMAIN_SENSITIVE_DATA_WITHOUT_POLICY for an entity classified at a level that requires a handling policy (personal, sensitive, secret, or regulated) when no datapolicy governs it.
Add the stable error code DOMAIN_CLASS_POLICY_CONFLICT for a data policy that governs an entity classified secret or regulated while declaring continuous export.

Add focused deterministic tests covering the endpoint-pair table, the new and extended relations, every governance rule with its negative cases, cross-phase ordering, no input mutation, and unchanged canonical revision identity.
Advance specs/CURRENT.md to record SG-000022 canonical closure and SG-000023 as the active frontier Grain.
scope_out: No new node kinds and no change to the classification or lifecycle vocabularies, required fields, or optional fields delivered by SG-000022.
No privacy, locale, external-effect, Dataset, design-system, skill, exploration-branch, or release semantics.
No Change Intent, proposed graph delta, Question Gate, Assumption Ledger, graph views, compiler, database, Supabase migration, or remote side effect.
No new workspace package, no new runtime dependency, no lockfile change, and no relaxation of existing rejection behavior or of endpoint compatibility for any existing edge kind.
No change to Product Graph v1 public contract semantics or to canonical revision identity for well-formed documents.
